attempts.error: OpenCV/PyTorch OpenMP runtime collision before epoch 1; replaced unsafe same-process preprocessing with a deterministic workspace cache.
Stopped during epoch 9 after a code audit found that early-stopping min_delta was incorrectly coupled to checkpoint selection; no test data had been opened.
Stopped during epoch 5 after runtime profiling showed that identical affine resampling could be batched on GPU; implementation-only optimization before any test access.
Stopped after epoch 1 to apply a benchmarked channels-last tensor layout; model, data, seeds, loss and all scientific hyperparameters remained unchanged and test was unopened.

The detached training process was terminated by the operating environment during epoch 24 (last validation-selected checkpoint: epoch 23). No Python exception was raised, so the trainer could not record the failure itself. No test data had been opened.

Deliberately terminated after epoch 2 to verify that the new epoch-boundary resume state restores an interrupted run. The restart resumed at epoch 3 and reproduced the pre-interruption validation losses exactly. No test data had been opened.

Aborted during epoch 30 by a console window-CLOSE event: 'forrtl: error (200): program aborting due to window-CLOSE event'. The detached launcher had created a visible console window, and the Intel Fortran runtime inside the numerical stack aborts the process when that window is closed. This is the same mechanism that terminated the earlier attempt. No Python exception was raised and no test data had been opened; epochs 1-29 survived in the resume state.
attempts.mitigation: Relaunched with no console window and with FOR_DISABLE_CONSOLE_CTRL_HANDLER=1 so console control events cannot abort the run; training resumes from the epoch-29 boundary.
